title: Semantic Caching (Redis/GPTCache)
summary: Reuse validated answers for sufficiently similar requests while preserving tenant, policy, freshness, and task boundaries.
overview: Semantic caching retrieves a previous answer by meaning rather than exact prompt bytes. It typically embeds the incoming query, searches cached query vectors, and applies an acceptance threshold before returning a stored response. The important contract is answer equivalence: two similar questions are not necessarily entitled to the same answer.

A cache entry must carry more than a vector and text. Tenant scope, authorization context, locale, model or prompt revision, source versions, and expiration determine eligibility. Personalized balances, changing prices, and action requests are usually poor candidates. Semantic caching differs from provider prefix caching, which reuses computation while still generating a fresh answer.

production.poc: A prototype measures hit quality on repeated public questions and labels false matches manually.
production.production: Production adds metadata gates, per-intent thresholds, invalidation, provenance, and a bypass for sensitive or volatile tasks.
production.scale: At enterprise scale, track false-hit rates by tenant and language, control cache cardinality, and test revocation propagation independently of expiration.

components.name: Eligibility classifier
components.role: Excludes personalized, action-oriented, or rapidly changing requests.

components.name: Embedding service
components.role: Maps eligible questions into a versioned similarity space.

components.name: Scoped vector cache
components.role: Stores answer evidence and filters entries by tenant and policy metadata.

components.name: Acceptance gate
components.role: Checks semantic threshold, freshness, and answer compatibility.

components.name: Generation path
components.role: Produces and validates fresh answers on a miss before storing eligible results.

flow.title: Check eligibility
flow.description: Determine whether answer reuse is allowed for the request type and data classification.

flow.title: Build scope
flow.description: Resolve tenant, language, policy revision, and source-version constraints.

flow.title: Search candidates
flow.description: Embed the question and retrieve nearby entries only within the allowed scope.

flow.title: Validate reuse
flow.description: Apply calibrated similarity and freshness checks; treat uncertainty as a miss.

flow.title: Generate on miss
flow.description: Run retrieval and generation, validate the answer, and retain its supporting evidence.

flow.title: Store and observe
flow.description: Write a bounded-life entry and measure hits, misses, false matches, and invalidation lag.

useCase.title: Repeated passenger policy questions
useCase.situation: A transit operator receives many paraphrases of the same baggage and bicycle questions.
useCase.problem: Repeated model calls answer stable policy questions while personalized journey requests share the interface.
useCase.requirement: Reuse policy answers without serving one passenger another passenger’s itinerary.
useCase.architecture: The cache permits public policy intents and keys eligibility by policy revision and service region.
runtime: A bicycle-policy question matches a validated answer for the same region.
A fare-balance question bypasses caching and reads the passenger account directly.
useCase.failure: When the policy changes, its revision invalidates old entries even if their similarity scores remain high.
useCase.impact: Track avoided generation work alongside false-hit rate and policy freshness; a higher hit rate is harmful if answer equivalence deteriorates.

tradeoffs.cost: Raises the chance of a confidently wrong cache hit.
Reduces hit rate and increases index cardinality.
Forces more generation on stable questions.

failures.detection: Evaluation finds opposite-intent paraphrases near one another.
failures.recovery: Add hard-negative tests and stricter intent compatibility.

failures.detection: Answer provenance references an inaccessible source revision.
failures.recovery: Invalidate by source identifier and recheck authorization on retrieval.

mistakes.fix: Calibrate thresholds using labeled answer-equivalence pairs.
Store only accepted responses with provenance.

mistakes.mistake: Sharing entries across users by default
mistakes.fix: Partition or gate reuse using explicit authorization scope.

whenToUse: Use for repeated stable informational questions.
Use where false hits can be evaluated with labeled examples.
Use when generation cost exceeds cache lookup overhead.
whenNotToUse: Avoid personalized balances and action requests.
Avoid rapidly changing facts without reliable invalidation.
Do not reuse answers across incompatible permissions.
checklist: Measure false hits as a first-class metric.
